items.title: George Henderson Interview, 1961-05-03
items.q: Mr. Redden? Mr. Redden. Mr. Redden.

ctx.x: You wet it. You sprinkle it and you wet it and it makes a paint. It colors the brick. You know what I mean? You put it on there with a little board and brush it with a little. Brick for a little. Hardware stove. I used to get it at the hardware stove. This is old. This must be about 15 or 20 years old. I bought it about a pound and you use very little of it. You don't need much to cover it. You would like a little bit for a sample? I'll get a little bit out of this.
I'll get a little bit out of this. Mr. Redden? Mr. Redden. Mr. Redden.

I thought I had, this was the brick bag but I used the brick up. You see? I've been had that. That must be about eight or nine years old because the little boy that bought that, he don't live here on his mother's day over six years or seven years. That little he is when he got that for my daughter. Mr. Redden.
